sources.citation: Franklin, Karl J. & C. L. Voorhoeve. 1973. Languages near the intersection of the Gulf, Southern Highlands and Western Districts. In K. J. Franklin (ed.), The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea (Pacific Linguistics C-26), 149-186. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress for Fiwaga. Section 4.22 'Phonemic Inventory' (pp. 154-155) compares Fasu and Foe phonemes and adds one sentence on Fiwaga (p. 155): 'Fiwaga apparently has no /t/ or /v/ phoneme; however, it shows two series of stops, as Foe, as well as a glottal phoneme.' Fiwaga otherwise appears only in the lexicostatistical tables (pp. 153-154: 64/60/60% with Foe) and the language legend (p. 182: 'FIWAGA (East Kutubuan) Beaver Falls'). Appendix C wordlists (pp. 557-560) cover Fasu, Foe, Kaluli, Kasua, Namumi, Bainapi -- no Fiwaga list. The word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the chap…
